snippet.title: How to Install Simple Cabinet Hardware | This First House
snippet.description:
Contractor Zack Dettmore shows a homeowner how to install simple cabinet hardware that can be adjusted for a perfect fit.

SUBSCRIBE to This Old House: http://bit.ly/SubscribeThisOldHouse.

With so many types of cabinet hardware available, it might seem more complicated than it is. But those cabinets with European hinges (also known as cup hinges) are simple to install and make adjusting the doors quick and easy. Contractor Zack Dettmore shows our homeowner, Jorge, how to install them and tweak them for a perfect fit.

Installing Cup Hinges in the Door
Half of a cup hinge fits inside a pre-drilled mortise in the cabinet door. Simply place it over the mortise and push down until it bottoms out in the mortise. In some cases, you’ll need to tighten two set screws, but even simpler designs exist that require simply closing a cover to secure them in place.

Cabinet Installation
The other half of the hinge is installed inside the cabinet. They install with just a few screws, the holes for which are usually pre-drilled in ready-to-assemble or pre-assembled cabinets.

snippet.title: Install Garage Ceiling Insulation | This First House
snippet.description:
In an attempt to save money on their renovation, first-time homebuyers Nick and Hannah tackle their garage insulation project themselves.

SUBSCRIBE to This Old House: http://bit.ly/SubscribeThisOldHouse.

When Nick and Hannah realized their new nursery would sit right above their attached garage, they had some concerns about noise and temperature control. In order to address both concerns, they knew garage insulation was a must-do project. To save money, they tackled the project on their own, installing mineral wool in their joist bays.

Wear the Proper PPE
Batts insulation is full of small fibers that become airborne and can cause itching. To avoid these annoyances, make sure to wear the proper personal protective equipment (PPE). This includes a respirator, safety glasses, gloves, and long sleeves.

Work With a Partner
Working with a partner can be a big help when installing insulation. One person can stay on the ladder and keep fitting the batts panels between the joists while the other cuts the panels to length and width. This is the most efficient workflow for tackling these projects.

Use Full-Length Batts Wherever Possible
When installing insulation in a garage ceiling, it’s best to use full-length batts wherever possible, avoiding as many seams as possible. If you have to cut, make sure to save the offcuts as they can be helpful with filling in any gaps and nooks.

Use a Layered Design
For the best results, use a double-layered design. This allows for more insulation and simplifies the installation. Make sure to stagger the joints of the layers so they don’t line up and allow air to pass through. This can make a significant difference in insulation performance.

It Can Be Like a Life-Sized Game of Tetris
Making sure that each piece of insulation is properly installed and fits the space carefully can feel like a big game of Tetris. But every gap must be filled properly to ensure all of the insulation can act as a system and prevent heat transfer.
